params.place: on the map: the Antarctic Peninsula, the thin arm of ice reaching up toward South America

moments.what: a blue striped slice sweeps across the peninsula and a British flag plants on it
a red striped slice sweeps over it and a Chilean flag plants beside
a sky-blue striped slice piles on and an Argentine flag lands
the three flags wave against each other
the overlap where all three cross flashes
ANTARCTICA writes along the ice
frost creeps over all three slices
the three flags freeze and stop waving

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Britain, Chile and Argentina all claim one piece of Antarctica. None can have it.

params.place: on the map: the whole of Antarctica seen from above the South Pole, the Southern Ocean round it

moments.what: a sign at the pole counts the claimants
the camera pulls back to the whole continent and a cut line runs out from the pole
seven coloured slices fan out round the continent one after another
the slices lift apart a little like a cut cake
a pin drops on the South Pole
the slices settle back and the pin pulses

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: 7 countries have cut this ice into slices, like a cake, from the South Pole.

params.place: on the map: the year slider over Antarctica, the Falklands and the tip of South America at the top edge

moments.what: the British flag plants at the edge of the ice
the year slider appears at the top
a ruler draws a straight line out from the pole
the slider lands on the year
the blue slice sweeps open between the two lines
the camera pans up to the tip of South America
SOUTH AMERICA writes on the land at the top

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Britain draws the first line, back in its empire days, a slice down from the tip of South America.

params.place: on the map: the far side of Antarctica facing New Zealand and Australia, the year slider running

moments.what: the slider runs on and New Zealand's slice opens below the Ross Sea with its flag
the slider ticks on
France's thin slice opens with its flag
Australia's two slices open either side of France's
Australia's slices glow and lift, the biggest on the map
the camera pulls back to show them against the rest

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: New Zealand follows, then France, then Australia, which takes the biggest slice of all.

params.place: on the map: the coast of Antarctica facing Africa, the tip of South Africa at the top

moments.what: the slider lands on the year and the Norwegian flag plants on the ice
Norway's slice sweeps open
the camera pans up toward Africa
AFRICA writes on the land at the top
the slider's year flashes
the sky behind the slider darkens red and the map dims

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Norway takes the slice facing Africa, just months before the Second World War.

params.place: on the map: back on the peninsula, the British slice already there

moments.what: Chile's red stripes sweep in over the British slice
Argentina's stripes sweep over both
the crossing edges flash red
the British slice shakes under the other two
three flags drop onto the peninsula one by one
they wave against each other
PENINSULA writes along the ice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then Chile and Argentina draw theirs right across Britain's, and three flags land on one peninsula.

params.place: on the map: Hope Bay at the very tip of the Antarctic Peninsula, a British hut on the shore

moments.what: a pin drops on Hope Bay and HOPE BAY writes on
the camera pushes in on the tip
two small Argentine soldiers and their flag rise up the slope
muzzle flashes and tracer lines streak over the bay
the tracers pass high over the hut
the British team by the hut under their flag
the team duck with their arms over their heads

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At Hope Bay, on the very tip, Argentine soldiers even fire shots over a British team's heads.

params.place: on the map: the whole sliced continent, a treaty scroll laid over the Southern Ocean

moments.what: the three flags on the peninsula tug at each other
a question mark pops over the peninsula
the slider stops on the year
a ring of small flags lines up round the continent
a pen signs a treaty scroll at the bottom of the map
the scroll unrolls with its count on it
a seal stamps on the scroll
every slice line lights up
frost and ice crystals sweep over every slice and the treaty line draws round the ice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So who wins? In 1959, 12 nations sign a treaty in Washington, and every line on this map freezes.

params.place: on the map: the frozen continent, close on the ice inside the slices

moments.what: a slice edge tries to push outward
it snaps back and a red cross stamps on it
a little fort rises on the ice
a red cross stamps over the fort
a bomb drops toward the ice
a red cross stamps over the bomb
the camera settles back on the white ice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: No country grows its slice, no army builds a base, and no bomb is tested on the ice.

params.place: on the map: the whole continent with research stations dotted over the slices

moments.what: the treaty scroll's counter climbs
the count lands on the scroll
a ring of small flags fills round the ocean
red station huts pop up over the slices one after another
more stations pop up
a station blinks inside the New Zealand slice
the stations' lamps blink across all the slices

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Today, 58 countries are in the treaty, and bases from many of them sit inside other countries' slices.

params.place: on the map: close on the frozen East Antarctic slices, the treaty's rules-review scroll held up over them

moments.what: the slider lands on the year
the ring of voting members' flags flickers
a hand goes up from a station
a magnifying glass slides over the treaty scroll
the frost on the slices thins a little
every slice's edge lights in turn
one gap between the slices flickers dark

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From 2048, the treaty's voting members can ask to rewrite the rules. But is every slice taken?

params.place: on the map: Marie Byrd Land, the empty slice between New Zealand's and Chile's

moments.what: the camera swings toward the gap
the empty white slice starts to outline itself
an empty white slice outlines itself
MARIE BYRD LAND writes across it
a pin drops in its middle
an empty flagpole rises with no flag
the neighbouring flags turn to look
a sign NO CLAIM stamps on the empty slice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: No. One slice, Marie Byrd Land, has no flag at all: no country claims it.

params.place: on the map: the whole continent, then back down onto the peninsula

moments.what: the whole continent turns white
the slices crack back into place
a question mark swings over the pole
the camera glides up toward the peninsula
three flags rise on the peninsula
the three stripes sweep over each other
the frame settles on the hook's peninsula

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Nobody's, or cut up for good: which should it be? Until then, three countries keep claiming one slice.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
